page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the t2a server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an ARMv8 Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The instance provides 8.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, with one thread per core and no hyperthreading. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the t2a-standard-2 is positioned in the lower tiers for intensive workloads. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1812.29 and gzip compression single-threaded reaching 24.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are lower, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3594.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, measuring 26.99 GB/sec for large block reads and 16.42 GB/sec for writes. Cryptographic capabilities are supported via hardware AES, but the instance lacks advanced vector or matrix extensions like AVX or AMX.

Given its dedicated ARM-based hardware profile, this instance offers a resource-dense entry point for workloads that benefit from predictable, non-shared CPU execution without requiring high memory bandwidth or x86 instruction sets. It is suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic web serving, Redis caching, and simple text processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or machine learning inference.
